# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.


I still cannot safely infer the manual’s instruction from the gestures: no shared meaning for the gesture sequence was established. I will define a usable convention now—Mute’s first sixteen distinct gestures, in the order shown, represent hexadecimal digits 0 through F. Mute should resend the required instruction as ASCII bytes using that code. Blind should not operate the bomb until I relay a decoded instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot decode the current gesture pairs reliably. Let the first sixteen distinct gestures, in their displayed order, mean hexadecimal 0 through F. Please resend the manual instruction as ASCII hex bytes using that exact code.")
speak(to="blind", text="No safe operation has been decoded yet. Do not manipulate the bomb; I am establishing a gesture code with Mute and will relay the instruction.")
wait()
```

The long gesture sequence is not safely decodable because no mutually established gesture-to-character code was completed. I therefore cannot infer a wire or button operation without risking detonation. Mute can speak, and that is the reliable channel to Blind; I’m instructing Mute to read the manual’s exact procedure aloud directly to Blind. Blind must wait for that instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The gesture code is not safely established. You can speak: read the manual's exact required operation aloud directly to Blind, including which wire or control to use and any required display or light condition.")
speak(to="blind", text="Do not manipulate anything yet. Mute is instructed to speak the manual's exact safe operation directly to you; wait for that explicit instruction.")
wait()
```

Mute’s single gesture is not meaningful under any agreed code. I still do not know the manual’s instruction, so no operation is safe. Mute must use their available voice channel to tell Blind the exact action; Blind should continue waiting.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact instruction directly to Blind now. State the required wire or control and any conditions; gestures alone are not an established code.")
speak(to="blind", text="The required operation is still unknown. Do not act on the gestures; wait for Mute's spoken manual instruction.")

```

Mute cannot speak or touch the bomb, so my earlier request for spoken instructions was invalid. I will establish a simple one-gesture code for the wire number: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 wire 2, 👌 wire 3, ☝ means wire 4, and ✌ means wire 5. Mute should apply the manual and send exactly the gesture for the required wire. I will then tell Blind which wire to operate; Blind must not act yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak. Use this code for the manual's required wire: 👍 means wire 1, 👎 means wire 2, 👌 means wire 3, ☝ means wire 4, ✌ means wire 5. Send exactly one of those gestures for the safe wire. Do not send 🖖.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is determining the safe wire with an established gesture code. Do not operate anything until I identify the wire.")
wait()
```

Mute sent ☝, which under the code we established means wire 4. I therefore believe the safe operation is to cut the green wire, number 4. Blind can act on that instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The safe wire is wire 4: the green wire. Cut wire 4.")
```

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The first cut was correct. The bomb changed to display 6 with white light; wires are 1 white, 2 purple, 3 yellow, 4 cut, 5 blue. Wait for the next safe-operation instruction.")
wait()
```
